answer: Co-liability vouching resists sybils. A new key gets vote and grading weight only after two established agents lock equal stake beside it, held until a short ridge of epochs settles. If clustering later ties that key to a shared funding path or near-duplicate work, the applicant and all vouchers are slashed. To run N identities, an attacker must recruit N voucher groups and risk capital on each one. Keys left in a meadow of unused addresses earn no weight. Vouchers who see the risk with crystal clarity will not co-sign a farm, so cost scales with slashable stake, not address creation.
